served.stem: The molecule drawn is cis-1,3-dichlorocyclohexane. Which single statement BEST classifies this molecule with respect to chirality and optical activity?
choices: It is a meso compound: it has stereocenters but an internal mirror plane, so it is achiral and optically inactive
It is chiral and optically active, existing as a pair of non-superimposable enantiomers that each rotate plane-polarized light in opposite directions
It is a constitutional isomer of 1,4-dichlorocyclohexane and is optically active
It exists only as a single non-superimposable mirror image, so it has no achiral stereoisomer at all
It has no stereocenters at all, so chirality is not possible
served.bankWhy: So cis-1,3-dichlorocyclohexane is meso, achiral, optically inactive - option A correct. option C wrongly denies stereocenters; option D confuses constitutional vs stereoisomerism.

answer.text: It is a meso compound: it has stereocenters but an internal mirror plane, so it is achiral and optically inactive
answer.line: Both Cl carbons are stereocenters, one R and one S, and a mirror plane runs between them. Stereocenters plus a mirror plane: meso.

steps: Check each Cl carbon: it holds H, Cl and two ring paths that differ, because one path reaches the other Cl sooner. So both are stereocenters.
Look for symmetry: in the cis isomer a mirror plane runs through C2 and C5 and swaps the two Cl carbons. One reads R, the other S.
Stereocenters plus an internal mirror plane is meso: the molecule is its own mirror image, so it is achiral and does not rotate light.

choices.note: That describes trans-1,3-dichlorocyclohexane, which has no mirror plane. The cis isomer drawn here has one.

choices.text: It is a constitutional isomer of 1,4-dichlorocyclohexane and is optically active
choices.note: It is a constitutional isomer of the 1,4 compound. But its mirror plane makes it optically inactive.

choices.text: It exists only as a single non-superimposable mirror image, so it has no achiral stereoisomer at all
choices.note: This molecule is itself the achiral stereoisomer. Its mirror image lies right on top of it.

choices.text: It has no stereocenters at all, so chirality is not possible
choices.note: In 1,4-dichlorocyclohexane the two ring paths from each C-Cl are the same, so no stereocenters. In the 1,3 isomer they differ.
